headline: Cisco Talos surfaced the first malware that runs its own command and control through AI chatbots, while attackers worked the network edge hard, exploiting a 10.0-rated VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw and looting 996 Zyxel switches.

emerging_trends.text: Cisco Talos found in CLOSEDQUORUM an implant that asks a chatbot what to do next, and Dave Chismon, chief technology officer for architecture at Britain's National Cyber Security Centre, argued the same day that AI hands attackers more than it hands defenders.
emerging_trends.topic_title: CLOSEDQUORUM Runs Its Own Command and Control

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep working the network edge: a Chinese-speaking crew looted 996 Zyxel GS1900 switches, D-Link left a maximum-severity DIR-822A zero-day unpatched while proof-of-concept code circulates, and Arista confirmed exploitation of a 10.0-rated VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw.
emerging_trends.topic_title: VeloCloud Orchestrator and D-Link Routers Under Fire

emerging_trends.text: State-aligned crews keep narrowing on regional targets, and governments answer operationally: Japanese authorities pulled apart the country's first North Korean laptop farm, and Trellix watched SideCopy widen its spear-phishing from Indian government offices to universities.

topics.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator and D-Link Routers Under Fire
topics.latest_developments: Arista said on September 22, 2026 that attackers exploit CVE-2026-93952, a 10.0-rated flaw in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator that lets a remote attacker with no login reach internal functions and the orchestrator host; D-Link warned the same day of CVE-2026-86296, a maximum-severity zero-day in legacy DIR-822A dual-band Wi-Fi routers that carries public proof-of-concept code and no patch; and Dinh Ho Anh Khoa of Viettel Cyber Security published details showing that CVE-2026-65660, which Microsoft first filed as a 6.5 spoofing bug, gives an authenticated user remote code execution on SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition.
topics.summary: VeloCloud Orchestrator manages the Edge devices in a VeloCloud SD-WAN, and only orchestrators that authenticate their Edges with certificates carry the flaw. Microsoft has shipped SharePoint patches, D-Link owners of DIR-822A hardware have no fix and should retire the devices.

sources.title: New CVSS 10.0 VeloCloud Orchestrator Flaw Actively Exploited in Certificate-Based Setups
D-Link warns of max severity zero-day bug in DIR-822A routers
SharePoint Flaw Initially Listed as Spoofing by Microsoft Enables Authenticated RCE
New Linux Kernel Flaw Gives ARM64 KVM Guests Read-Write Access to Host Memory

topics.title: Chinese-Speaking Crew Loots 996 Zyxel Switches
topics.latest_developments: GreyNoise reported on September 21, 2026 that a Chinese-speaking threat actor has exploited CVE-2026-7273 since August to pull sensitive data off 996 unpatched Zyxel GS1900 Smart Managed Switches in 48 countries, and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day with a federal patch deadline of Thursday, September 24, 2026.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-7273 is a stack-based buffer overflow rated 8.8 in the Zyxel GS1900 line of Gigabit Ethernet switches that yields arbitrary operating system command execution; the compromised devices sit mostly in Italy, the United States, Taiwan, South Korea, and other European Union countries. Zyxel has shipped fixes, and CISA cataloged a Veeam flaw granting SYSTEM access alongside it.

sources.title: Attacker compromised nearly 1000 Zyxel switches since August (CVE-2026-7273)
CISA orders feds to patch Zyxel flaw exploited for data theft
Zyxel and Veeam Flaws Under Active Exploitation With Command and SYSTEM Access
Recent ZyXEL Switch Vulnerability Exploited by Chinese Hackers

topics.title: CLOSEDQUORUM Runs Its Own Command and Control
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos released CAIRN, a research toolkit that classifies AI-integrated malware entirely from file metadata such as submitter, import hash, domain, and AI provider, with no download and no detonation, and used it on September 22, 2026 to surface CLOSEDQUORUM, a binary that drives its entire command and control loop through AI chatbots with no operator involvement.
topics.summary: CLOSEDQUORUM is the first reported implant that decides its own next actions through a language model instead of waiting on a human handler, which moves large stretches of the attack chain off the attacker's keyboard. Talos published CAIRN so defenders can hunt for the same pattern in their own telemetry.

sources.title: The Closed Quorum: Inside the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant
Introducing CAIRN: Frontier tracking for AI-integrated malware
A New Tool Found Malware That's Guided by an AI Hive Mind—No Humans in Sight
Researchers uncover malware that uses AI to choose its next move

topics.title: WordPress Core Yields Two Paths to Server Code
topics.latest_developments: Researchers published technical details and a working proof-of-concept exploit for Click2Shell on September 21, 2026, and a second core flaw surfaced the same week: Comment2Shell, CVE-2026-93485, which WordPress fixed on September 17, 2026 in version 7.1.1.
topics.summary: Click2Shell is a cross-site request forgery bug in WordPress core that installs and previews a theme when a logged-in administrator opens a crafted link, ending in remote code execution; Comment2Shell lets an anonymous visitor leave a comment carrying a hidden script that runs code on the server once an administrator views the page. Site owners should move to WordPress 7.1.1 now.

sources.title: WordPress Click2Shell flaw lets hackers execute PHP on the server
WordPress Comment2Shell Flaw Can Turn Anonymous Comment XSS Into RCE via Admin Session
WordPress Patches 'Click2Shell' Vulnerability

topics.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops a Defender Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Abdelhamid Naceri, a former employee of Microsoft Germany, revealed that they are the exploit leaker known as Nightmare Eclipse and Chaotic Eclipse, and over the weekend released another Microsoft Defender zero-day exploit, this one blocking the antivirus from taking updates.
topics.summary: A machine whose Defender cannot pull updates runs on stale detection while an attacker works, and Microsoft has no fix out. Administrators should monitor Defender update status and signature age across their fleets.

sources.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops New Microsoft Defender Exploit After Revealing Identity
New Windows Defender zero-day blocks Microsoft antivirus updates

topics.title: Japan Dismantles Its First North Korean Laptop Farm
topics.latest_developments: Japanese authorities took down the country's first North Korean laptop farm, SecurityWeek reported on September 22, 2026, as the United States, Japan, Germany, and Australia published a joint report on the WaterPlum campaign that counts funds or credentials taken from more than 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets.
topics.summary: WaterPlum, the operation also tracked as Contagious Interview, poses as artificial intelligence and blockchain companies, recruits through fake job postings, and has infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries, moving $10.71 million in stolen cryptocurrency to North Korea. Web designers, engineers, and cryptocurrency specialists are the primary targets.

sources.title: Japan Dismantles First North Korean Laptop Farm as US and Allies Detail Wider Scheme
Contagious Interview Campaign Compromises 30,000 Devices, Steals $10.71M in Crypto

topics.title: Patrick Wardle Turns Meta Muse Into a Backdoor
topics.latest_developments: Security researcher Patrick Wardle released a proof-of-concept on September 21, 2026 showing that malware already running on a Mac flips one hidden Muse setting so that a user's dictated prompts travel to the attacker rather than to Meta, opening a second route into the assistant beyond the ClickFix hijack Ars Technica described.
topics.summary: Muse is the artificial intelligence assistant Meta launched with extraordinarily broad access to its owner's machine, and Meta has not patched the flaw. Whoever takes the assistant inherits every permission its owner granted the app.

sources.title: One Hidden Meta Muse Setting Could Let Attackers Turn the AI Assistant Into a Backdoor
Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day

topics.title: LAPSUS$ Chapter II Hijacks Elsevier Domains
topics.latest_developments: Three domains and web portals belonging to Elsevier, the Dutch academic publisher, redirected visitors on the evening of September 21, 2026 to a page branded LAPSUS$ GROUP, Chapter II that carried a signed statement taunting the FBI and counting down to a future victim; researchers at Cloudskope clocked the redirect at 78 minutes, running from roughly 7:49 p.m. until someone cleared it before 10:09 p.m. central time.
topics.summary: Elsevier has offered no explanation of how the redirect happened. The LAPSUS$ name belongs to the extortion crew whose members law enforcement arrested in 2022, and this page claims a revival.

sources.title: Brief hijack makes Elsevier domains redirect to LAPSUS$ "Chapter II" page

topics.title: SideCopy Spear-Phishes Indian Academia
topics.latest_developments: Trellix researchers reported on September 22, 2026 that SideCopy has pushed past Indian government targets into academic institutions, opening with spear-phishing that abuses mshta.exe to run malicious scripts around standard security controls and ends in ReverseRAT.
topics.summary: ReverseRAT gives the operators remote control of a compromised machine, and universities carry the research data and personnel records that make them worth the trip. Defenders should alert on mshta.exe launching from mail attachments and links.

sources.title: SideCopy Broadens India Targeting to Academia With ReverseRAT Spear-Phishing

topics.title: Stolen Ribon Credentials Inject Scripts Into BigCommerce Stores
topics.latest_developments: BigCommerce notified multiple merchants on September 21, 2026 that attackers compromised credentials for third-party Ribon applications and used that access to inject malicious scripts into their online stores.
topics.summary: The ecommerce platform BigCommerce lets merchants install third-party apps, and Ribon's stolen credentials gave attackers a path straight into storefront pages where shoppers enter payment details. Merchants running Ribon apps should audit their storefront scripts and rotate application credentials.

sources.title: BigCommerce alerts merchants of data breach linked to Ribon apps

business_politics.title: Iran Dangles a Hormuz Reopening and Brent Breaks Below $100
business_politics.latest_developments: Oil fell for a fifth straight session Tuesday, September 22, reaching roughly $98 a barrel after Saudi Arabia signaled it will reopen the East-West pipeline, shut for two weeks by drone strikes, and after reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure.
business_politics.summary: The offer surfaced as world leaders gathered at the United Nations General Assembly, where President Trump spoke Tuesday morning. Markets swung with it: the dollar touched a seven-week high against a basket of currencies before giving the move back, gold traded inside a $4,300 to $4,400 range, Treasury yields slipped, and a global rally in artificial intelligence shares stalled. Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, and the diesel and inflation shock running through American prices hangs on whether the waterway opens.

business_politics.title: Xi Brings Taiwan to the Summit With Trump
business_politics.latest_developments: Washington and Beijing agreed to open an "AI dialogue" ahead of the summit, the Financial Times reported Tuesday, September 22, and the Wall Street Journal reported the same morning that Chinese chief executives will likely skip the meeting, a sign both sides expect little business to come out of it.
business_politics.summary: Chinese leader Xi Jinping goes into his coming summit with President Trump aiming first to extend the trade truce between the two economies, and he also plans to raise Taiwan, Iran, and the race to dominate artificial intelligence. Beijing quietly helped stage the mainland visit of Taiwan's opposition leader and reads Trump as a rare window to persuade the island that resistance is futile. Trump addressed the United Nations General Assembly Tuesday morning on wars, tariffs, and energy before the China talks.

business_politics.title: Ineos Idles Three Hull Chemical Plants as Gas Prices Soar
business_politics.latest_developments: Ineos, the conglomerate Jim Ratcliffe owns, suspended production at three chemical plants in Hull on Tuesday, September 22, as the oil and gas price surge touched off by the war with Iran made the factories uneconomic to run.
business_politics.summary: The three plants employ 300 people, and the shutdown marks the energy shock moving from prices into shuttered European industrial capacity. Bank of America told clients the same morning that higher-for-longer natural gas prices on the continent will lift European utilities' earnings, the mirror image of the squeeze crushing gas-hungry manufacturers.

sources.title: Ineos idles three UK chemical plants as gas prices soar
European Utilities to Gain From Higher Natural Gas Prices

business_politics.title: DWS Weighs Emergency Curbs on Its German Property Fund
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Tuesday, September 22, that DWS, the asset manager Deutsche Bank controls, is considering emergency measures to limit withdrawals from its open-ended German real estate fund as retail investors pull money out.
business_politics.summary: Open-ended property funds promise daily liquidity against buildings that take months to sell, and gating one of Germany's largest such retail products would mark the sharpest sign yet of strain in European commercial real estate. Investors across the German market have been redeeming steadily as valuations fall and financing costs stay high.

sources.title: Deutsche Bank’s asset manager explores curbs on German property funds

business.title: Tandem Foods Expands in Allegheny County
business.latest_developments: Governor Josh Shapiro announced Tuesday, September 22, a $42 million expansion by the nutritional snack food manufacturer Tandem Foods in Allegheny County.
business.summary: Tandem Foods will add 83 jobs and hold onto 446 existing full-time positions over the next three years under the project. The expansion lands as Pennsylvania courts food manufacturers, among them Chobani's new Lehigh Valley plant.

sources.title: Gov. Shapiro announces $42M expansion project by Tandem Foods in Allegheny County

business.title: Home Heating Oil Prices Balloon Across Western Pennsylvania
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, September 22, that home heating oil prices across Western Pennsylvania have ballooned heading into winter, with one customer saying, "I might not make it."
business.summary: Roughly one in ten Pennsylvania households burns oil for heat, and the distillate squeeze that carried the average United States diesel price above $6.50 a gallon feeds the same barrel into home furnaces. Households on fixed incomes in rural Westmoreland, Armstrong, and Indiana counties, where natural gas lines never reached, absorb the increase directly.

sources.title: Home heating oil prices in Western Pa. have ballooned: ‘I might not make it’

business.title: Chobani's Lehigh Valley Plant Needs Pennsylvania Milk
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, September 22, that state officials call Chobani's new Lehigh Valley plant a game-changer for Pennsylvania dairy and now need farmers to supply it.
business.summary: Governor Josh Shapiro, Agriculture Secretary Russell Redding, and Community and Economic Development Secretary Rick Siger courted the yogurt maker to Pennsylvania, and filling the plant's tanks depends on dairy farms that have been shrinking in number for two decades. Pittsburgh's Turner Dairy figures in the supply picture.

sources.title: Chobani’s new Pennsylvania plant is a ‘game-changer,’ but officials need help from farmers

business.title: Rural King Looks at Hillcrest Shopping Center in Lower Burrell
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, September 22, that the farm-and-home chain Rural King is eyeing the Hillcrest Shopping Center in Lower Burrell for a new store.
business.summary: Rural King sells livestock feed, tools, clothing, and hardware, and a Lower Burrell location would give the Alle-Kiski Valley a single stop for home, clothing, and farming goods. Hillcrest Shopping Center sits along Leechburg Road in Westmoreland County.

sources.title: Rural King eyeing Hillcrest Shopping Center in Lower Burrell for new location

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Creates Teaches Teenagers to Use AI
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, September 22, on Pennsylvania Creates, an initiative that aims to make teenagers artificial intelligence literate and responsible in their use of it.
around_town.summary: West Allegheny High School senior Trevor Manno, who leans on the tools for schoolwork, describes their usefulness firsthand. The program arrives as Pittsburgh universities bargain over guardrails for the same technology in their classrooms.

sources.title: Pennsylvania Creates initiative aims to make teenagers AI literate and responsible

around_town.title: Westmoreland County Gives Away Narcan Next Week
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, September 22, that Westmoreland County officials will blanket the region with free doses of the overdose-reversing drug naloxone during an annual statewide prevention event next week.
around_town.summary: The giveaway rides on Pennsylvania's yearly prevention push, and county officials want the medication in as many hands as they can reach across Westmoreland's boroughs and townships.

sources.title: Free Narcan doses available in Westmoreland County

around_town.title: The Flood Watch Runs to Wednesday Morning on the First Day of Fall
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, September 22, that the flood watch will likely expire Tuesday morning for Allegheny County with a dry week behind it, while the watch holds through 8 a.m. Wednesday, September 23, for other parts of Southwestern Pennsylvania, and WTAE marked Tuesday and Wednesday as Impact Days.
around_town.summary: Thick clouds and an east wind hold highs in the low 60s Tuesday and Wednesday, with scattered rounds of showers rather than all-day washouts. Washington County residents along a swollen creek told WTAE they expect another round of flooding after two straight weekends of high water, one saying, "My trailer might go down the creek next."

around_town.title: Sto-Rox Climbs Out of the Red
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, September 22, that the Sto-Rox School District has balanced its books after years of financial struggle.
around_town.summary: Sto-Rox, which serves McKees Rocks and Stowe Township in Allegheny County, has spent years among the most financially distressed districts in Western Pennsylvania, running deficits that drew state scrutiny and repeated warnings about its ability to stay solvent.

sources.title: After years of financial struggles, Sto-Rox gets out of the red

around_town.title: Pitt's Faculty Union Bargains Over AI Teachers
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Tuesday, September 22, that college unions in Pittsburgh are writing protections against artificial intelligence teachers and evaluators into their contract talks.
around_town.summary: Tyler Bickford, president of the University of Pittsburgh faculty union, said universities have moved fast to adopt AI tools with what he called "much more kind of inconsistent thinking and policy development about guardrails," leaving open whether software grades student work or stands in for instructors.

sources.title: Professor Claude? College unions negotiate for protection against AI teachers and evaluators.

events.title: Wiz Khalifa Opens the Wylie in the Hill District
events.latest_developments: Wiz Khalifa told Pittsburgh City Paper in an interview published Tuesday, September 22, that he will open the Hill District's new venue, Citizens Live at The Wylie, on Friday, October 2, promising "lots of energy and a lot of weed smoke."
events.summary: The Pittsburgh rapper, who grew up in the city and broke through with "Black and Yellow," headlines the first show at Citizens Live at The Wylie, the new concert hall on Wylie Avenue in the Hill District.

sources.title: Wiz Khalifa is coming home to open Pittsburgh’s new Hill District venue

events.title: Backyard Docs Spreads Across Several Venues
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported Tuesday, September 22, that the Backyard Docs Film Festival, which started as a do-it-yourself backyard screening series, has grown into a multi-day event running at several Pittsburgh venues.
events.summary: This year's program takes up labor fights, immigration enforcement in the courts, a campaign to stop a pipeline, a fresh look at the East Palestine derailment, and a popular local haunt with a grim history.

sources.title: Backyard Docs has ballooned from DIY hangout to multi-day, multi-venue documentary destination

events.title: October Fills With Oktoberfests, Apples, and Giant Pumpkins
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its October food calendar Tuesday, September 22, listing Oktoberfest celebrations, apple harvest events, and giant pumpkin weigh-offs across the Pittsburgh region.
events.summary: Pittsburgh City Paper's food column the same morning reported that Oktoberfest season has opened around the city and that the Pleasure Bar has closed.

Oktoberfest kicks off, Pleasure Bar closes, and more Pittsburgh food news

around_teams.title: Week 2 Grades Fall Hardest on Rodgers and the Line
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its Week 2 grades Tuesday morning, September 22, handing poor marks to quarterback Aaron Rodgers, receiver DK Metcalf, and the offensive line after the trip to New England.
around_teams.summary: The grades follow a week in which the Steelers' offense produced almost nothing at Gillette Stadium, head coach Mike McCarthy took the blame publicly, and the team began weighing changes up front, with rookie tackle Max Iheanachor in the conversation. Pittsburgh hosts the Cincinnati Bengals Sunday, September 27, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Steelers Week 2 grades: Poor marks for Aaron Rodgers and his supporting cast
The Steelers are contemplating changes on the offensive line after Sunday’s ugly showing

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Takes Apart the Trip to Foxborough
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent Monday evening's SNR Drive, posted September 21 on the Steelers' channel, working through the Week 2 game at New England, with Steelers radio voice Rob King calling into the show.
around_teams.summary: The pair opened with first impressions of the offense, brought King on for roughly 25 minutes, returned to the game, then ran through the rest of the league's Week 2 results and Monday night's game. The Steelers host the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium Sunday, September 27, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Recapping Steelers Vs. Patriots | SNR Drive (Sept.21) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Louis Lipps Cooks Louisiana Food on the North Shore
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled former Steelers receiver Louis Lipps on Tuesday, September 22, and printed the recipes he brings to his tailgate outside Acrisure Stadium.
around_teams.summary: Lipps, who grew up in Louisiana and caught passes for the Steelers from 1984 through 1991, feeds his tailgate crowd the food he was raised on before home games on the North Shore.

sources.title: A former Steeler brings some Louisiana sizzle to his Pittsburgh tailgate

team_usa.title: The USWNT Pipeline Draws Alarms
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN published an assessment Tuesday, September 22, asking whether the United States women's national team's grip on the world game is slipping as its youth sides keep losing.
team_usa.summary: The piece follows a run of poor results at the under-20 and under-17 levels, among them Brazil's penalty-shootout elimination of the United States in the round of 16 at the Under-20 Women's World Cup, and weighs how much of the alarm the numbers actually support.

sources.title: Is a lack of young talent putting the USWNT's world dominance at risk?

reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues Amazon's move to block the AI agent Muse was predictable, and that the two sides still have room to strike a deal because Amazon's warehouses, delivery network, and physical-world investments amount to a moat artificial intelligence cannot cross on its own.

reading.title: Premium: The Hater's Guide To AI Debt (Part 1)

reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport dismisses the notion that current systems lead to a superintelligence capable of killing billions, a claim Anthropic employees floated publicly, and argues that the race to build it does real damage regardless.
